content: 1. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, cobimetinib should be resumed at a dose of 60 mg. For patients on reduced doses of cobimetinib (40 mg or 20 mg daily), alternative medications to moderate CYP3A inhibitors should be considered. 2. Colestipol reduces tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only for oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 3. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 4. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Conversely, metronidazole can also increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of cortisone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Crofelemer increases tetracycline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Crofelemer may inhibit CYP3A4 at gut concentrations but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. 8. Cyclophosphamide increases tetracycline levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 9. Metronidazole increases cyclosporine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. Dabrafenib decreases tetracycline levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Tetracycline enhances the effects of dalteparin through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 12. Danazol increases tetracycline levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 13. Metronidazole increases dapsone levels or effects by affecting both CYP2E1 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 14. Tetracycline increases daridorexant levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Daridorexant doses should not exceed 25 mg per night when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Metronidazole increases darifenacin levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Metronidazole increases darunavir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Metronidazole increases dasatinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 18. Metronidazole increases deflazacort levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Deflazacort doses should be reduced to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be used. 20. Metronidazole increases dexamethasone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Metronidazole increases diazepam levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 22. Tetracycline increases diazepam levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Dichlorphenamide increases bismuth subsalicylate levels through an unknown mechanism. Co-administration is contraindicated. High-dose aspirin with dichlorphenamide may increase salicylate levels, leading to anorexia, tachypnea, lethargy, and coma. 24. Metronidazole increases diclofenac levels or effects by altering CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 25. Tetracycline reduces dicloxacillin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Alternative drugs should be used. 26. Didanosine decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Oral tetracycline should not be administered simultaneously with didanosine chewable tablets or oral solution powder. 27. Didanosine and metronidazole may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially enhancing the risk of peripheral neuropathy. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 28. Metronidazole increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Tetracycline increases digoxin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Metronidazole increases dihydroergotamine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 31. Metronidazole increases disopyramide levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 32. Disulfiram increases metronidazole toxicity by reducing its metabolism, leading to enhanced CNS and cardiac toxicity. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Metronidazole increases docetaxel levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 34. Metronidazole increases donepezil levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 35. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs should be used. 36. Metronidazole increases dronabinol toxicity by inhibiting aldehyde dehydrogenase. Co-administration is contraindicated. Metronidazole should be discontinued at least 14 days before starting dronabinol solution and not administered within 7 days of completing dronabinol treatment. 37. Metronidazole increases dronedarone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 38. Drospirenone increases tetracycline levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 39. Metronidazole increases dutasteride levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 40. Efavirenz decreases tetracycline levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, metronidazole increases efavirenz levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 41. Tetracycline increases elacestrant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Metronidazole also increases elacestrant levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 42. Elagolix decreases tetracycline levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 43. Metronidazole increases eletriptan levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Tetracycline increases eliglustat levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Metronidazole also increases eliglustat levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors are not recommended with eliglustat poor or intermediate metabolizers. For extensive metabolizers, reduce eliglustat dose from 84 mg BID to 84 mg once daily. 45. Bismuth subsalicylate and eluxadoline may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of constipation-related adverse reactions. Alternative drugs should be used. 46. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases tetracycline levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates associated with serious or life-threatening events. 47. Encorafenib affects tetracycline metabolism by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Tetracycline enhances enoxaparin effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 49. Tetracycline increases entrectinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Metronidazole also increases entrectinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous entrectinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 50. Enzalutamide decreases tetracycline levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 51. Metronidazole increases eplerenone levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 52. Metronidazole increases ergotamine levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 53. Metronidazole increases erlotinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Metronidazole increases erythromycin base levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 55. Metronidazole increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 56. Metronidazole increases erythromycin lactobionate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 57. Metronidazole increases erythromycin stearate levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 58. Bismuth subsalicylate and esmolol may interact through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially causing severe hypertension by blocking renal prostaglandin synthesis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Esomeprazole increases bismuth subsalicylate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 60. Metronidazole decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Conversely, metronidazole can also increase estradiol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Tetracycline decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Caution and monitoring are advised. 62. Tetracycline increases estradiol vaginal levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Metronidazole also increases estradiol vaginal levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
